mobile.doctor.watches.ok.role: Diagnostics check result (CLI, desktop, pasted into support)
mobile.doctor.watches.ok.note: Doctor check sentence for `lop mobile doctor` and the desktop's Copy diagnostics (Linux only), read by a non-technical user. It reports the per-user Linux inotify budget, which has two separate limits: a 'file watch' is one watched folder (inotify watch, limit fs.inotify.max_user_watches; when it runs out programs fail with 'No space left on device'), and a 'watch handle' is one inotify instance a program opens to hold its watches (limit fs.inotify.max_user_instances; when it runs out programs fail with 'Too many open files'). Keep the two terms clearly distinct from each other. Numeric placeholders are pre-formatted numbers and {pid} is a process id; {name} is the program's own process name (for example 'Local Operator' or 'systemd') and stays verbatim; {command} is a literal shell command (for example lop services restart or systemctl --user restart foo.service) and stays verbatim. {how} picks one of three arms: 'command' when a restart command is known (names {name}, {pid} and {command}), 'program' when only the holder is known (names {name} and {pid}; restart that program by hand), and 'other' when the holder is unknown (no holder clause, only the administrator fix; {name}, {pid} and {command} are empty and must not appear). Keep all three arms, and start each arm with a word, not {name}. fs.inotify.* are system setting names and stay verbatim; the quoted English error messages are what other programs print and stay verbatim inside the locale's quotation marks.
